newsitem.title: UK: Mark crosses drift as market focuses on sterling.
newsitem.headline: Mark crosses drift as market focuses on sterling.

text.p: The mark drifted against its European crosses at Europe's midday as the currency market focused on the British pound's continued assault on the mark.
Amid a lack of eye-catching news on the European monetary union front or the German economy and a holiday in the U.S. today, dealers said there was little to trade on.

There was some interest in Italy as optimism over the nation's EMU convergence sent the BTP futures market to record highs and shrank the ten-year yield spread between benchmark BTPs and Bunds to a record low of 101 basis points.
Italian inflation data out today added to this optimism, with June CPI up 1.4 percent on the year compared with 1.6 percent in May and 3.9 in June last year.
Traders said this fuelled expectations for more Italian rate cuts in the near future, but that the lira failed to respond.

"Maybe that's only natural as the lira's had a very good run recently. In fact we're expecting a bit of a correction in the lira but the market doesn't seem to have the energy now," said one trader at a Japanese bank here.
Mark/lira was at 973.55/85 at 1120 GMT against its late Thursday levels of 973.11/31.

"The lira's trading on a forward basis now, with people looking at the forward rate for the beginning of EMU in 1999. That should leave the spot lira well supported as long as Italy doesn't cut interest rates too fast," said one economist at a U.S. fund management group here.
Comments by Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing on German interest rates failed to stir the market, with traders saying the remarks offset each other.
Issing said there was no need for an interest rate hike right now, and also said a further rate cut would be counterproductive in the current economic environment.
He also said there were no signs of tensions concerning exchange rates when asked about the strength in dollar/mark, which rose to a 40-month high on Thursday.
Outside the European crosses group, the mark dropped sharply against the yen, falling close to the 20-month low of 64.66 yen reached in June.
"But the mark/yen drop hasn't affected the European crosses today because it was more of a yen-buying move rather than mark weakness," the Japanese bank trader said.

Meanwhile, the Nordic currencies firmed on the mark. Mark/Swedish crown fell to 4.3905, its lowest since late February, compared with 4.4070/1.00 on Thursday. Mark/Norway was trading at its lowest in nearly a month at 4.1620/30 against 4.1720 at Thursday's close.
